primary_claim: ISaeRFT (Interpretable Sparse Autoencoder Representation Fine Tuning) — a technique that gradient-optimizes IA3-style learned scaling factors on SAE latents via a HuggingFace PeftModel — has a working prototype where DPO loss decreases significantly within as few as 20 training steps, though the research is at a very early stage with no major proof of concept yet on downstream tasks.

effect.value: DPO loss goes down significantly in as few as 20 steps

stated_future_work: hyperparameter search, e.g. trying a larger Adam beta2 to account for sparse gradients
compare with baselines: what fraction of IA3's performance can ISaeRFT recover with a constant number of parameters
train with more complicated ISaeRFT components such as a feed-forward neural network
apply ISaeRFT to attention, and switch to using Sparse Crosscoders since their features are more global throughout the model
run an experiment reversing preferences for one behavior type (e.g. vulgarity) in a preference dataset to see if the technique can spot the unwanted changes
limitations_stated: status is very early days of the research, with no major proof of concept yet
having a HuggingFace trainer evaluate the model during training is not currently available for peft models; a workaround is still needed
no established way yet to measure the distance of edits in the residual stream, since SAE latents activate at different frequencies and magnitudes
quote: DPO loss goes down significantly in as few as 20 steps.
